Modbus.Title: Veton EV Charger
Modbus.Comment: Veton / Phoenix Contact CHARX over Modbus TCP - charging point 1 (registers 1xxx)

ModbusCmd.Title: Charging release mode
ModbusCmd.Comment: Release mode (X120): 0 Dashboard,1 Whitelist,2 External,3 Permanent,4 OCPP,5 Modbus

ModbusCmd.Title: SOC
ModbusCmd.Comment: Vehicle state of charge (X264), if reported

ModbusCmd.Title: Vehicle status
ModbusCmd.Comment: IEC 61851 vehicle status (X299): two ASCII chars packed in one register - A1=16689 A2=16690 B1=16945 B2=16946 C1=17201 C2=17202 D1=17457 D2=17458 E0=17712 F0=17968 IN=18766. Vehicle connected (B/C/D) = 16945..17458.

ModbusCmd.Title: Last RFID card
ModbusCmd.Comment: Last RFID card UID as ASCII text (X275): the UID of the card last presented, e.g. 14 hex characters for a 7-byte card, 8 for a 4-byte card. The charger exposes 10 holding registers, big-endian, NUL-padded. Sticky: keeps the previous card until a DIFFERENT card is tapped (the same card again = no change). Verified in OCPP release mode on firmware 1.7.3 only. Feed it to the Wallbox block's Uid (User ID) input so the charge log carries the card holder; the UID is personal data, hide the input from non-admin users. Confirm in Loxone Config that exactly the full UID shows (how many registers the String type reads is undocumented): fewer characters = short read, extra characters after the UID or the input offline = more than 10 registers, spilling into X285-X294 - report either.

ModbusCmd.Title: Max Charging Rate I
ModbusCmd.Comment: Set max charging current in A (X301)
ModbusCmd.HintText: Set the max amount of amps that the car is able to use. Feed it amps from a kW→A formula (see README), never the Wallbox block's kW output directly. 0 = pause (charging release withdrawn); re-sent every 60 s by RepeatRate

ModbusCmd.Title: Watchdog fallback current
ModbusCmd.Comment: CHARX safety watchdog fallback current in A (X306), range 6-80: the current the charger falls back to when the X307 watchdog timer expires
ModbusCmd.HintText: Current the charger drops to if the Miniserver stops writing (X307 expires). Set 6 A so a lost Miniserver slows the car down instead of cutting it off. A value outside 6-80 A withdraws the charging release.

ModbusCmd.Title: Watchdog timer
ModbusCmd.Comment: CHARX safety watchdog timer in s (X307): re-write within this interval to keep it alive; 65535 disables the watchdog
ModbusCmd.HintText: Deadline in seconds. The charger falls back to X306 if it is not written again within this time. Keep it fed with RepeatRate (60 s here, five re-sends of margin on a 300 s timer). Write 65535 to disable the watchdog.
